sanskrit: rājyabhāgī dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ prāpnuyān nāpadaṃ naraḥ nakṣatre vāruṇe kurvan bhiṣaksiddhim avāpnuyāt
english: He who performs the śrāddha under Dhaniṣṭhā becomes a sharer in kingdoms and meets with no calamity; performing it under the lunar mansion of Varuṇa, a man attains success in the healing art.

sanskrit: pūrvaproṣṭhapadāḥ kurvan bahu vinded ajāvikam uttarāsv atha kurvāṇo vindate gāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Performing it under the Pūrva-Proṣṭhapadā stars, he gains goats and sheep in abundance; performing it under the Uttarā stars, he gains cattle by the thousand.

sanskrit: bahurūpyakṛtaṃ vittaṃ vindate revatīṃ śritaḥ aśvāṃś cāśvayuje vetti bharaṇīṣv āyur uttamam
english: Resorting to Revatī, he gains wealth wrought of much silver; under Aśvayuj he obtains horses, and under the Bharaṇī stars the highest length of life.

sanskrit: imaṃ śrāddhavidhiṃ śrutvā śaśabindus tathākarot akleśenājayac cāpi mahīṃ so 'nuśaśāsa ha
english: Having heard this ordinance of the śrāddha, Śaśabindu acted accordingly; without hardship he conquered the earth, and he ruled it.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśebhyaḥ pradātavyaṃ bhavec chrāddhaṃ pitāmaha dvijebhyaḥ kuruśārdūla tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: To brāhmaṇas of what sort should the śrāddha-offering be given, O grandsire? O tiger of the Kurus, you ought to expound this to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇān na parīkṣeta kṣatriyo dānadharmavit daive karmaṇi pitrye tu nyāyyam āhuḥ parīkṣaṇam
english: Bhīṣma said: A kṣatriya versed in the law of giving should not scrutinize brāhmaṇas in rites for the gods; but in the rite for the ancestors, scrutiny is held to be proper.

sanskrit: devatāḥ pūjayantīha daivenaiveha tejasā upetya tasmād devebhyaḥ sarvebhyo dāpayen naraḥ
english: The deities here honor the offering by their divine splendor when they draw near; therefore a man should have the offering given to all the gods alike.

sanskrit: śrāddhe tv atha mahārāja parīkṣed brāhmaṇān budhaḥ kulaśīlavayorūpair vidyayābhijanena ca
english: But at the śrāddha, O great king, the wise man should examine the brāhmaṇas by their family, character, age, and form, by their learning and noble birth.

sanskrit: eṣām anye paṅktidūṣās tathānye paṅktipāvanāḥ apāṅkteyās tu ye rājan kīrtayiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇu
english: Of these, some are defilers of the row and others are sanctifiers of the row; those who are unworthy of the row, O king, I shall now name—hear of them.

sanskrit: kitavo bhrūṇahā yakṣmī paśupālo nirākṛtiḥ grāmapreṣyo vārdhuṣiko gāyanaḥ sarvavikrayī
english: The gambler, the slayer of an embryo, the consumptive, the cattle-herder, the misshapen, the village drudge, the usurer, the professional singer, the seller of every kind of ware,

sanskrit: agāradāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī sāmudriko rājabhṛtyas tailikaḥ kūṭakārakaḥ
english: the house-burner, the poisoner, the eater of food in a vessel of adultery's child, the seller of soma, the seafarer, the king's servant, the oil-presser, the forger of false coin,

sanskrit: pitrā vivadamānaś ca yasya copapatir gṛhe abhiśastas tathā stenaḥ śilpaṃ yaś copajīvati
english: he who quarrels with his father, he in whose house there is a paramour, the man falsely accused, the thief, and he who lives by a manual craft,

sanskrit: parvakāraś ca sūcī ca mitradhruk pāradārikaḥ avratānām upādhyāyaḥ kāṇḍapṛṣṭhas tathaiva ca
english: the maker of festival days, the informer, the betrayer of friends, the adulterer, the teacher of those without vows, and likewise the renegade who turns his back on his own kindred,

sanskrit: śvabhir yaś ca parikrāmed yaḥ śunā daṣṭa eva ca parivittiś ca yaś ca syād duścarmā gurutalpagaḥ kuśīlavo devalako nakṣatrair yaś ca jīvati
english: he who roams about with dogs, he who has been bitten by a dog, he who marries before an elder brother, the man of diseased skin, the defiler of his teacher's bed, the actor-dancer, the temple-priest who lives off idols, and he who lives by reading the stars—

sanskrit: etān iha vijānīyād apāṅkteyān dvijādhamān śūdrāṇām upadeśaṃ ca ye kurvanty alpacetasaḥ
english: these one should know to be unworthy of the row, the basest of the twice-born, together with those of little wit who give instruction to śūdras.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ kāṇaḥ śataṃ ṣaṇḍhaḥ śvitrī yāvat prapaśyati paṅktyāṃ samupaviṣṭāyāṃ tāvad dūṣayate nṛpa
english: A one-eyed man defiles sixty, a eunuch a hundred, O king; and a man with white leprosy, when seated in the row, defiles as far as his eye can reach.

sanskrit: yad veṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yad bhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ sopānatkaś ca yad bhuṅkte sarvaṃ vidyāt tad āsuram
english: What is eaten with the head wrapped, what is eaten facing south, and what is eaten while still shod—all this one should know to belong to the demons.

sanskrit: asūyatā ca yad dattaṃ yac ca śraddhāvivarjitam sarvaṃ tad asurendrāya brahmā bhāgam akalpayat
english: What is given grudgingly and what is given without faith—all this Brahmā has apportioned as the share of the lord of the asuras.

sanskrit: śvānaś ca paṅktidūṣāś ca nāvekṣeran kathaṃ cana tasmāt parivṛte dadyāt tilāṃś cānvavakīrayet
english: Dogs and defilers of the row should by no means look upon the offering; therefore one should give it in an enclosed place and scatter sesame seeds around it.

sanskrit: tilādāne ca kravyādā ye ca krodhavaśā gaṇāḥ yātudhānāḥ piśācāś ca vipralumpanti tad dhaviḥ
english: When the sesame offering is omitted, the flesh-eating fiends, the hosts driven by wrath, the yātudhānas, and the piśācas plunder that oblation.

sanskrit: yāvad dhy apaṅktyaḥ paṅktyāṃ vai bhuñjānān anupaśyati tāvat phalād bhraṃśayati dātāraṃ tasya bāliśam
english: For as long as one unfit for the row gazes upon those eating in the row, so long does he strip the foolish giver of his reward.

sanskrit: ime tu bharataśreṣṭha vijñeyāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ ye tv atas tān pravakṣyāmi parīkṣasveha tān dvijān
english: But these, O best of the Bharatas, are to be known as sanctifiers of the row; those who are such I shall now declare—examine these brāhmaṇas here.

sanskrit: vedavidyāvratasnātā brāhmaṇāḥ sarva eva hi pāṅkteyān yāṃs tu vakṣyāmi jñeyās te paṅktipāvanāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas who have completed their study of the Veda and their vows of the bath are, every one, worthy of the row; and those whom I shall name as worthy should be known as sanctifiers of the row.

sanskrit: triṇāciketaḥ pañcāgnis trisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit brahmadeyānusaṃtānaś chandogo jyeṣṭhasāmagaḥ
english: He who has thrice kindled the Nāciketa fire, the keeper of the five fires, the knower of the Trisuparṇa hymn, the master of the six Vedāṅgas, he born of a line of brahma-given marriages, the chanter of the Sāman, the singer of the Jyeṣṭha-sāman,

sanskrit: mātāpitror yaś ca vaśyaḥ śrotriyo daśapūruṣaḥ ṛtukālābhigāmī ca dharmapatnīṣu yaḥ sadā vedavidyāvratasnāto vipraḥ paṅktiṃ punāty uta
english: he who is obedient to his mother and father, the learned man of ten generations of Veda-knowers, and he who always approaches his lawful wives only in their season—such a brāhmaṇa, accomplished in Veda, learning, and vow, indeed purifies the row.

sanskrit: atharvaśiraso 'dhyetā brahmacārī yatavrataḥ satyavādī dharmaśīlaḥ svakarmanirataś ca yaḥ
english: The student of the Atharvaśiras, the chaste one of restrained vows, the speaker of truth, he of righteous conduct, and he who is devoted to his own appointed duty—

sanskrit: ye ca puṇyeṣu tīrtheṣu abhiṣekakṛtaśramāḥ makheṣu ca samantreṣu bhavanty avabhṛthāplutāḥ
english: and those who have toiled in ritual bathing at holy fords, and who have been bathed in the final ablution of sacrifices accompanied by their proper mantras—

sanskrit: akrodhanā acapalāḥ kṣāntā dāntā jitendriyāḥ sarvabhūtahitā ye ca śrāddheṣv etān nimantrayet eteṣu dattam akṣayyam ete vai paṅktipāvanāḥ
english: those free of anger, free of fickleness, patient, self-controlled, masters of their senses, and devoted to the welfare of all beings—these one should invite to the śrāddhas; what is given to them is imperishable, for these indeed are sanctifiers of the row.

sanskrit: ime pare mahārāja vijñeyāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ yatayo mokṣadharmajñā yogāḥ sucaritavratāḥ
english: These others too, O great king, are to be known as sanctifiers of the row: the ascetics who know the law of liberation, the men of yoga of well-practiced vows,

sanskrit: ye cetihāsaṃ prayatāḥ śrāvayanti dvijottamān ye ca bhāṣyavidaḥ ke cid ye ca vyākaraṇe ratāḥ
english: those who, intent and pure, recite the ancient lore to the best of the twice-born, those who are versed in commentary, and those who delight in grammar,

sanskrit: adhīyate purāṇaṃ ye dharmaśāstrāṇy athāpi ca adhītya ca yathānyāyaṃ vidhivat tasya kāriṇaḥ
english: those who study the Purāṇa and the treatises on dharma as well, and who, having studied them duly and rightly, act according to their precepts,

sanskrit: upapanno gurukule satyavādī sahasradaḥ agryaḥ sarveṣu vedeṣu sarvapravacaneṣu ca
english: he who has dwelt completely in his teacher's household, the speaker of truth, the giver of a thousand gifts, the foremost in all the Vedas and in all the recitations—

sanskrit: yāvad ete prapaśyanti paṅktyās tāvat punanty uta tato hi pāvanāt paṅktyāḥ paṅktipāvana ucyate
english: as far as these gaze upon the row, so far do they purify it; and because of this purifying of the row, each is called a sanctifier of the row.

sanskrit: krośād ardhatṛtīyāt tu pāvayed eka eva hi brahmadeyānusaṃtāna iti brahmavido viduḥ
english: Even a single such man, born of a line of brahma-given marriages, can sanctify the offering from a distance of two and a half krośas—so the knowers of Brahman declare.

sanskrit: anṛtvig anupādhyāyaḥ sa ced agrāsanaṃ vrajet ṛtvigbhir ananujñātaḥ paṅktyā harati duṣkṛtam
english: If one who is neither officiating priest nor teacher takes the foremost seat unauthorized by the officiants, he carries off, along with the row, only ill-deserved demerit.

sanskrit: atha ced vedavit sarvaiḥ paṅktidoṣair vivarjitaḥ na ca syāt patito rājan paṅktipāvana eva saḥ
english: But if he is a knower of the Veda, free of all the faults of the row, and is not a fallen man, O king, then he is indeed a sanctifier of the row.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena parīkṣyāmantrayed dvijān svakarmaniratān dāntān kule jātān bahuśrutān
english: Therefore with all care one should examine and invite brāhmaṇas devoted to their own duties, self-controlled, well-born, and deeply learned.

sanskrit: yasya mitrapradhānāni śrāddhāni ca havīṃṣi ca na prīṇāti pitṝn devān svargaṃ ca na sa gacchati
english: He whose śrāddhas and oblations are devoted chiefly to friends gratifies neither the ancestors nor the gods, and he does not attain to heaven.

sanskrit: yaś ca śrāddhe kurute saṃgatāni; na devayānena pathā sa yāti sa vai muktaḥ pippalaṃ bandhanād vā; svargāl lokāc cyavate śrāddhamitraḥ
english: He who turns the śrāddha into a gathering of friends does not travel by the path of the gods; like a fig loosed from its stalk, the man who befriends at the śrāddha falls away from the world of heaven.

sanskrit: tasmān mitraṃ śrāddhakṛn nādriyeta; dadyān mitrebhyaḥ saṃgrahārthaṃ dhanāni yaṃ manyate naiva śatruṃ na mitraṃ; taṃ madhyasthaṃ bhojayed dhavyakavye
english: Therefore the performer of the śrāddha should not honor a friend with it; let him give his friends wealth to win their goodwill instead. Whom he regards as neither foe nor friend, that neutral man let him feed at the rites for gods and ancestors.

sanskrit: yathoṣare bījam uptaṃ na rohen; na cāsyoptā prāpnuyād bījabhāgam evaṃ śrāddhaṃ bhuktam anarhamāṇair; na ceha nāmutra phalaṃ dadāti
english: As seed sown in barren ground does not sprout, and the sower of it gains no return on his seed, so the śrāddha eaten by the unworthy yields its fruit neither here nor hereafter.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hy anadhīyānas tṛṇāgnir iva śāmyati tasmai śrāddhaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hi bhasmani hūyate
english: For a brāhmaṇa who has not studied dies down like a fire of straw; to him the śrāddha should not be given, for no oblation is poured upon ashes.

sanskrit: saṃbhojanī nāma piśācadakṣiṇā; sā naiva devān na pitṝn upaiti ihaiva sā bhrāmyati kṣīṇapuṇyā; śālāntare gaur iva naṣṭavatsā
english: The mere feeding of friends is a fee fit for piśācas; it reaches neither the gods nor the ancestors. Drained of merit, it wanders here below, like a cow within the stable that has lost its calf.

sanskrit: yathāgnau śānte ghṛtam ājuhoti; tan naiva devān na pitṝn upaiti tathā dattaṃ nartane gāyane ca; yāṃ cānṛce dakṣiṇām āvṛṇoti
english: As clarified butter poured upon a fire that has died reaches neither the gods nor the ancestors, so too is what is given to dancing and to singing, and the fee one bestows upon one who knows no sacred verse.

sanskrit: ubhau hinasti na bhunakti caiṣā; yā cānṛce dakṣiṇā dīyate vai āghātanī garhitaiṣā patantī; teṣāṃ pretān pātayed devayānāt
english: The fee given to one who knows no sacred verse destroys them both and nourishes neither; deadly and contemptible, in its falling it casts the departed of such men down from the path of the gods.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ samayaṃ nityaṃ ye caranti yudhiṣṭhira niścitāḥ sarvadharmajñās tān devā brāhmaṇān viduḥ
english: Those who ever observe the discipline of the seers, O Yudhiṣṭhira, steadfast and knowers of all dharma—the gods know such brāhmaṇas to be true.

sanskrit: svādhyāyaniṣṭhā ṛṣayo jñānaniṣṭhās tathaiva ca taponiṣṭhāś ca boddhavyāḥ karmaniṣṭhāś ca bhārata
english: The seers are to be understood as devoted to recitation, devoted to knowledge, devoted to austerity, and devoted to ritual action, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kavyāni jñānaniṣṭhebhyaḥ pratiṣṭhāpyāni bhārata tatra ye brāhmaṇāḥ ke cin na nindati hi te varāḥ
english: The ancestral offerings are to be entrusted to those devoted to knowledge, O Bhārata; and among them, whatever brāhmaṇas there be who revile no one—those are the most excellent.

sanskrit: ye tu nindanti jalpeṣu na tāñ śrāddheṣu bhojayet brāhmaṇā ninditā rājan hanyus tripuruṣaṃ kulam
english: But those who revile others in their chatter—one should not feed them at the śrāddhas; for brāhmaṇas reviled, O king, can destroy a family through three generations.

sanskrit: vaikhānasānāṃ vacanam ṛṣīṇāṃ śrūyate nṛpa dūrād eva parīkṣeta brāhmaṇān vedapāragān priyān vā yadi vā dveṣyāṃs teṣu tac chrāddham āvapet
english: The word of the Vaikhānasa seers is heard, O king: from afar should one examine the brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Veda, and whether they be dear or hateful, in them should one set the śrāddha.

sanskrit: yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ bhojayed anṛcāṃ naraḥ ekas tān mantravit prītaḥ sarvān arhati bhārata
english: Though a man should feed a thousand thousands of men who know no sacred verse, a single knower of the mantras, when pleased, outweighs them all, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kena saṃkalpitaṃ śrāddhaṃ kasmin kāle kim ātmakam bhṛgvaṅgirasake kāle muninā katareṇa vā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By whom was the śrāddha first conceived, at what time, and of what nature? In the age of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, by which of the two sages was it ordained?

sanskrit: kāni śrāddheṣu varjyāni tathā mūlaphalāni ca dhānyajātiś ca kā varjyā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: What things are to be shunned in the śrāddhas, and what roots and fruits, and what kind of grain is to be avoided? Tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathā śrāddhaṃ saṃpravṛttaṃ yasmin kāle yad ātmakam yena saṃkalpitaṃ caiva tan me śṛṇu janādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: How the śrāddha came into being, at what time, of what nature, and by whom it was conceived—hear this from me, O lord of men.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvo 'triḥ kauravya paramarṣiḥ pratāpavān tasya vaṃśe mahārāja dattātreya iti smṛtaḥ
english: There was Atri, son of the Self-existent, O Kauravya, a supreme seer of mighty splendor; in his line, O great king, was born he remembered as Dattātreya.

sanskrit: dattātreyasya putro 'bhūn nimir nāma tapodhanaḥ nimeś cāpy abhavat putraḥ śrīmān nāma śriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Dattātreya had a son named Nimi, rich in austerity; and to Nimi there was born a son named Śrīmān, endowed with glory.

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasrānte sa kṛtvā duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ kāladharmaparītātmā nidhanaṃ samupāgataḥ
english: At the close of a full thousand years, having performed hard austerities, his being overtaken by the law of time, he came to his death.

sanskrit: nimis tu kṛtvā śaucāni vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā saṃtāpam agamat tīvraṃ putraśokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: But Nimi, having performed the purifications by the rite ordained, fell into bitter grief, wholly given over to sorrow for his son.

sanskrit: atha kṛtvopahāryāṇi caturdaśyāṃ mahāmatiḥ tam eva gaṇayañ śokaṃ virātre pratyabudhyata
english: Then, having made the funeral offerings on the fourteenth day, the great-minded one, brooding upon that very grief, awoke at the close of night.

sanskrit: tasyāsīt pratibuddhasya śokena pihitātmanaḥ manaḥ saṃhṛtya viṣaye buddhir vistaragāminī
english: As he awoke, his self veiled by grief, having drawn his mind back from the objects of sense, his understanding ranged far and wide.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcintayām āsa śrāddhakalpaṃ samāhitaḥ yāni tasyaiva bhojyāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: Then, composed in mind, he pondered the ordinance of the śrāddha—what foods, what roots, and what fruits had been dear to his son,

sanskrit: uktāni yāni cānyāni yāni ceṣṭāni tasya ha tāni sarvāṇi manasā viniścitya tapodhanaḥ
english: and whatever others were prescribed, and whatever were beloved of him—all these the man rich in austerity determined in his mind.

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ mahāprājña viprān ānāyya pūjitān dakṣiṇāvartikāḥ sarvā bṛsīḥ svayam athākarot
english: On the night of the new moon, O greatly wise one, having summoned brāhmaṇas and honored them, he himself fashioned all the seats of grass coiled toward the right.

sanskrit: sapta viprāṃs tato bhojye yugapat samupānayat ṛte ca lavaṇaṃ bhojyaṃ śyāmākānnaṃ dadau prabhuḥ
english: Then he brought forward seven brāhmaṇas together to the meal, and the lord gave them food of wild millet, with everything save salt.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāgrās tato darbhā viṣṭareṣu niveśitāḥ pādayoś caiva viprāṇāṃ ye tv annam upabhuñjate
english: Then darbha grasses, their tips pointing south, were laid upon the seats and at the feet of the brāhmaṇas who were partaking of the food.

sanskrit: kṛtvā ca dakṣiṇāgrān vai darbhān suprayataḥ śuciḥ pradadau śrīmate piṇḍaṃ nāmagotram udāharan
english: And having set the darbhas with their tips toward the south, well-disciplined and pure, he offered the rice-ball to Śrīmān, pronouncing his name and lineage.

sanskrit: tat kṛtvā sa muniśreṣṭho dharmasaṃkaram ātmanaḥ paścāttāpena mahatā tapyamāno 'bhyacintayat
english: Having done this, that best of sages, tormented by great remorse at the confounding of dharma he had wrought, fell to thinking:

sanskrit: akṛtaṃ munibhiḥ pūrvaṃ kiṃ mayaitad anuṣṭhitam kathaṃ nu śāpena na māṃ daheyur brāhmaṇā iti
english: "What is this I have performed, never done by the sages before? How may the brāhmaṇas not consume me with their curse?"

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcintayām āsa vaṃśakartāram ātmanaḥ dhyātamātras tathā cātrir ājagāma tapodhanaḥ
english: Then he called to mind the founder of his own line; and no sooner was he thought upon than Atri, rich in austerity, came near.

sanskrit: athātris taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā putraśokena karśitam bhṛśam āśvāsayām āsa vāgbhir iṣṭābhir avyayaḥ
english: Then Atri, seeing him so wasted with sorrow for his son, the imperishable one comforted him deeply with kindly words:

sanskrit: nime saṃkalpitas te 'yaṃ pitṛyajñas tapodhanaḥ mā te bhūd bhīḥ pūrvadṛṣṭo dharmo 'yaṃ brahmaṇā svayam
english: "O Nimi, this rite for the ancestors has been conceived by you, O man of austerity. Let no fear be yours: this dharma was foreseen of old by Brahmā himself.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ svayaṃbhuvihito dharmaḥ saṃkalpitas tvayā ṛte svayaṃbhuvaḥ ko 'nyaḥ śrāddheyaṃ vidhim āharet
english: This dharma, ordained by the Self-existent, has been conceived by you; for save the Self-existent, who else could have set forth this ordinance of the śrāddha?

sanskrit: ākhyāsyāmi ca te bhūyaḥ śrāddheyaṃ vidhim uttamam svayaṃbhuvihitaṃ putra tat kuruṣva nibodha me
english: And I shall declare to you further the most excellent ordinance of the śrāddha, ordained by the Self-existent, O son; perform it, and mark my words.

sanskrit: kṛtvāgnikaraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ mantrapūrvaṃ tapodhana tato 'ryamṇe ca somāya varuṇāya ca nityaśaḥ
english: Having first performed the fire-rite with its proper mantras, O man of austerity, then ever offer to Aryaman, to Soma, and to Varuṇa;

sanskrit: viśvedevāś ca ye nityaṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha gocarāḥ tebhyaḥ saṃkalpitā bhāgāḥ svayam eva svayaṃbhuvā
english: and to those All-gods who ever range together with the ancestors—for them the shares were appointed by the Self-existent himself.

sanskrit: stotavyā ceha pṛthivī nivāpasyeha dhāriṇī vaiṣṇavī kāśyapī ceti tathaivehākṣayeti ca
english: And here the Earth is to be praised, she who upholds the offering—called the Vaiṣṇavī, the Kāśyapī, and likewise the Imperishable.

sanskrit: udakānayane caiva stotavyo varuṇo vibhuḥ tato 'gniś caiva somaś ca āpyāyyāv iha te 'nagha
english: And at the bringing of water, the all-pervading Varuṇa is to be praised; thereafter Agni and Soma are here to be gratified, O sinless one.

sanskrit: devās tu pitaro nāma nirmitā vai svayaṃbhuvā ūṣmapāḥ sumahābhāgās teṣāṃ bhāgāḥ prakalpitāḥ
english: The gods named the Fathers were indeed fashioned by the Self-existent, those drinkers of vapor of exceeding blessedness; for them the shares were apportioned.

sanskrit: te śrāddhenārcyamānā vai vimucyante ha kilbiṣāt saptakaḥ pitṛvaṃśas tu pūrvadṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā
english: Honored by the śrāddha, they are released from sin; the ancestral line is sevenfold, as foreseen of old by the Self-existent.

sanskrit: viśve cāgnimukhā devāḥ saṃkhyātāḥ pūrvam eva te teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi bhāgārhāṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: And the All-gods, fire-faced, were reckoned of old; I shall declare the names of those great-souled ones who are worthy of a share.
